metas.name: The Wages of Fear
metas.description: Because you watched Sorcerer: the 1953 Clouzot original: desperate men, trucks of nitroglycerine and unbearable tension.

metas.name: The Look of Silence
metas.description: Because you watched The Act of Killing: Oppenheimer's companion piece, as a victim's brother quietly confronts the men who killed him.

metas.name: Meantime
metas.description: Because you watched Made in Britain: Tim Roth again, alongside Gary Oldman's skinhead, in Mike Leigh's East End dole drama.

metas.name: Ratcatcher
metas.description: Because you watched Fish Tank: Lynne Ramsay's debut: a Glasgow boy during the 1970s bin strike, poetic and piercing, Kes-like in its tenderness.

metas.name: Samurai Rebellion
metas.description: Because you watched Harakiri: Kobayashi and Nakadai again, now with Mifune defying his clan in a slow-boiling revolt that ends in a superb duel.

metas.name: The Friends of Eddie Coyle
metas.description: Because you watched The French Connection: Robert Mitchum's small-time Boston gunrunner squeezed by cops and crooks; the most lived-in crime film of the 70s.

metas.name: Night Moves
metas.description: Because you watched Chinatown: Gene Hackman's LA private eye drifts into a murky Florida Keys mystery, the other great 70s neo-noir.

metas.name: McCabe & Mrs. Miller
metas.description: Because you watched Deadwood: Altman's muddy, snowbound frontier town is Deadwood's spiritual ancestor.

metas.name: The Night Comes for Us
metas.description: Because you watched The Raid 2: Timo Tjahjanto pits Joe Taslim against Iko Uwais; possibly the most brutal action film ever made.

metas.name: Four Lions
metas.description: Because you watched Peep Show: co-written by Peep Show's Jesse Armstrong and Sam Bain with Chris Morris; a jihadi farce that's hilarious and horrifying.
